profile.summary: A SEQC2 study that built a high-confidence set of somatic copy number gains, losses and loss-of-heterozygosity (LOH) regions for the hyper-diploid breast cancer cell line HCC1395, and used it to score six CNV callers on whole-genome and whole-exome tumour and normal sequencing under varied conditions. The truth set comes from agreement across 21 WGS replicates and six callers (five for LOH), checked against microarrays and Bionano. It is useful to cancer genomics groups choosing a CNV caller or validating a somatic CNV pipeline.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Results, 'Study design' and 'Establishment of CNV reference call set'

summary_quotes.text: This study rigorously evaluated six CNV callers: ascatNgs, CNVkit, FACETS, DRAGEN, HATCHet, and Control-FREEC.

High-confidence CNV clusters in the cancer cell line were defined by the consensus scores across 21 WGS replicates with six callers (126), in combination of supporting evidence from three orthogonal technologies, Affymetrix CytoScan, Illumina Array, and Bionano.
Only five callers detected LOH: CNVkit, Control-FREEC, DRAGEN, FACETS, and HATCHet, resulting in 105 call sets (21 replicates × 5 callers).

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: How reproducibly and accurately somatic CNV callers detect copy gain, copy loss and LOH in a cancer genome whose ploidy is not two (HCC1395 ploidy 2.85), and how sequencing centre, WGS versus WES, FFPE fixation, tumour purity, read coverage, DNA input and library protocol change the result.

quotes.text: whose genome ploidy was determined as 2.85

The WGS on tumor sample purity (SPP) dataset, comprising varying tumor and normal gDNA mixtures with tumor purities ranging from 5 to 100% and different read coverage amounts (ranging from 10 to 300X coverage).
The FFPE samples dataset, which included four time points for fixing time in both WGS and WES analyses.

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: For gains and losses, six callers were run on 21 fresh tumour and matched normal WGS replicates from six sequencing centres, giving 126 call sets. LOH calls come from the five callers that report LOH (CNVkit, Control-FREEC, DRAGEN, FACETS, HATCHet), giving 105 call sets, with their own score cut-offs for the confidence levels. Overlapping calls were split into disjoint intervals and scored for reproducibility within centre, across centres and across callers, then given strong, medium, weak or neutral confidence. The benchmark keeps strong-evidence calls and medium or weak calls supported by at least two of three orthogonal technologies (Affymetrix CytoScan, Illumina BeadChip, Bionano); neutral calls are excluded. The paper reports 346 gain calls (1525.6 Mb), 33 loss calls (87.9 Mb) and 320 LOH calls (1490.4 Mb). The deposited BED file holds 307 gain intervals (1503.9 Mb, counted from the saved file) against the paper's 346; its 33 loss and 320 LOH rows match the paper.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: A call set is scored by genomic overlap with the high-confidence set: precision is the fraction of called CNV regions that match, recall the fraction of high-confidence regions that are called, and F1 their harmonic mean, computed with BEDTools. Reproducibility between call sets uses the Jaccard index of region lengths. Chr6p, chr16q, chrX and gap regions are excluded. The authors state that only the qualitative class (gain, loss, LOH) is benchmark-grade; copy number values and breakpoints are not.

quotes.text: Precision is the fraction of CNV-affected regions of a query set which are the same with high-confident calls’ regions. Recall is the fraction of CNV-affected regions of high-confidence calls which are called by a query set. F1 score is the harmonic mean of the precision and recall.
The Jaccard index was utilized to evaluate the reproducibility or similarity of two scall sets.
CNVs on the p-arm of chr6, q-arm of chr16, chrX, and gap regions (including centromere regions and telomere regions) were excluded from this analysis.

The copy number calls which were derived from the median of called values by six callers should not be used as “gold-standard” for benchmarking study. In addition, break points of CNV segment were the best estimate and thus imprecise.

facts.value: None in the machine learning sense. The truth set is built from the same callers that are then scored (six for gains and losses, five for LOH), with orthogonal array and Bionano support required for medium and weak calls.

quotes.text: The CNV benchmark sets comprised strong-evidence calls and medium/weak- evidence calls supported by at least two of the three orthogonal technologies. Neutral-evidence calls were excluded from the benchmark set.

facts.label: Uncertainty
facts.value: Replicates across centres and callers are the main measure of variability; precision and recall are shown per replicate in figures. No confidence intervals are given for caller accuracy.

notes: Count mismatch worth a human look: the paper prints 346 gain, 33 loss and 320 LOH calls (699 in all), and its Discussion says CNV (688). The deposited ngs_benchmark_cnvs_gain_loss_loh.bed has 660 rows: 307 gain, 33 loss and 320 LOH (counted by Rewire from the saved file). The structured sizes use the paper's numbers. The paper names ascatNgs v2.5.1 in its methods text but 4.2.1 in its methods table. The record has no protocols or results in the store.
